# Cloud's three whole-project readers have NO multi-page test — the same class fixed three times on DC

## Claim

`adapters/jira/acli_graph.py`'s `get_parent_map`, `get_comment_map` and `get_issuelinks_map` each
paginate a whole project through an opaque `nextPageToken` cursor at `page_size = 100`. **No test
exercises more than ONE page.** The only coverage,
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_acli_cross_mixin_binding.py:188,200`, feeds payloads
carrying `"isLast": True` — a single page, terminating immediately.

This is the SAME defect class that shipped three times on the DC/shared side and was fixed each
time only after it was found in production-shaped code:
  * change 1105 — `get_parent_map` advanced by the REQUESTED page size and stopped on a short page;
  * [rebar:9263-b404-cb6c-463f] — `get_issuelinks_map` and `get_comment_map`, the same bug;
  * [rebar:deac-4f5a-856a-49bd] — `fetcher._iter_pages`, which lost 92% of a snapshot when measured.
The Cloud copies of these three readers have never been tested past their first page.

## Why the risk is real rather than theoretical

* The cursor contract is genuinely stateful: `acli_graph.py:271-272` terminates on `isLast` OR on a
  null/absent `nextPageToken`, and the request echoes the token back at `:225`. Nothing asserts the
  cursor ADVANCES, that a second page is fetched and merged, that a null token stops the loop, or
  that a repeated token cannot spin forever.
* A silent truncation here is invisible: these are whole-project READS feeding the differ, so the
  symptom is missing parents / comments / links, not an error.
* DC now has exactly these tests (`test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py:66-128`, recovering 250
  items from a 20-cap client) plus a structural AST guard at `:166`. **That guard scans the DC
  transport source only**, so a fourth unpaginated caller cannot be added silently on DC and CAN be
  on Cloud.
* Live coverage does not compensate: the live Cloud tier exercises a real project, but nothing pins
  the working set above 100 issues, so a passing live run is not evidence the cursor loops.

NOTE the fetcher-level guard is NOT this. `fetch/test_fetcher_truncation_gate.py` covers the
FETCHER's search loop (same-token-twice / offset-stall). These three `acli_graph` readers are a
separate code path with a separate cursor.

## Provenance

Found by a Cloud-vs-DC test-parity audit commissioned while closing epic e369, not by a failure.
The audit's framing is worth keeping: the DC side has been heavily tested recently, so the parity
gap runs in BOTH directions — this is the largest instance of Cloud lacking what DC now has.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] a test drives each of `get_parent_map`, `get_comment_map`, `get_issuelinks_map` against a
      fake ACLI client whose working set EXCEEDS one page, and asserts EVERY item is recovered —
      a count comparison against the seeded set, not a `> 0` floor
- [x] the cursor is asserted to ADVANCE: the second request carries the token the first response
      returned, asserted on the recorded request bodies
- [x] termination is asserted on BOTH documented conditions independently — `isLast: True`, and a
      null/absent `nextPageToken`
- [x] a repeated cursor token does NOT loop forever (mirrors the fetcher's same-token-twice guard);
      it either raises or stops, and the test pins which
- [x] each new test is MUTATION-CHECKED: breaking the loop after the first page must turn it RED,
      recorded on this ticket with the verdicts
- [x] the structural anti-regression guard is extended to cover `adapters/jira/acli_graph.py`, so a
      fourth unpaginated whole-project reader cannot be added silently on EITHER deployment
